subject.title: [Bug] QQ Bot: skill_workshop approval "Allow" button always recorded as rejected

question: Should a QQ Bot direct C2C callback resolve privileged approvals solely because it occurred in a private conversation, without an explicit non-wildcard approver or command allowlist entry?
rationale: Current documentation and merged security hardening require explicit actor authority, while the linked PR intentionally relaxes that boundary; available evidence does not establish that every C2C sender is the trusted operator.

options.title: Preserve explicit authorization
options.body: Keep the current boundary and add actionable denial UX plus focused configuration guidance for legitimate users.

options.title: Bind approval to owner identity
options.body: Permit implicit C2C approval only when the callback actor matches a stable configured owner or trusted request-origin identity, backed by live QQ proof and regression tests.

options.title: Trust every direct conversation
options.body: Adopt the linked PR's policy that any non-group callback supplies sufficient approval authority despite open or wildcard DM access.

recommendation.title: Preserve explicit authorization
recommendation.body: Keep the current boundary and add actionable denial UX plus focused configuration guidance for legitimate users.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history connects this person to the command-authorization alignment and merge decision establishing the current QQ Bot approval boundary.
